defect: After denying the notification permission and returning to the level-up hub, re-tapping the notifications CTA goes straight back to the hub instead of showing anything — no permission popup, no explanation.
hypothesis: Once permission is 'denied', the browser will not re-show the native prompt: Notification.requestPermission() resolves immediately with 'denied'. NotificationScreen unconditionally called enableDailyReminder() then onDone(), so it silently no-op'd and bounced back to the hub. The browser cannot re-prompt a denied permission, so the correct fix is to detect the denied state and surface the existing (previously unused) 'blocked' guidance telling the user to re-enable in browser settings instead of navigating away.
note: Fix lands in NotificationScreen UI, which plan.json marks out-of-scope for MS-1 (the serviceWorker.ready timeout). Change is localized: a pure decision helper (notificationCtaAction) in the existing notification-onboarding model plus a small branch in NotificationScreen.handleRequest. The 'denied' i18n string already existed in en/fr but was never wired up. No DOM/testing-library harness exists, so the decision logic was extracted to a pure, unit-tested function rather than fabricating a component test.
